CURRICULUM VITAE

Tomislav Mesarić
Ulica Lipa 12, 10000 Zagreb, Croatia | +385 1 555 0142 | tomislav.mesaric@example.com

PROFILE
Butcher with 9 years of experience in high-street and market butchery. Experienced in breaking down beef, pork and lamb carcasses, cutting to order, making fresh sausages, advising customers and maintaining clean, safe counters. Holds a vocational butcher certificate and a basic HACCP food hygiene certificate.

RELEVANT EXPERIENCE

Butcher | Mesnica Kod Ante (family butcher shop), Zagreb | 2019–present
• Break down 2–3 beef forequarters and 10–12 pork sides per week; bone, trim and portion meat for the counter.
• Make four kinds of fresh sausage to the shop’s recipes, including ćevapi, kobasice, chipolata and lamb merguez; produce about 40 kg per week in the busy season.
• Rotate cold-room stock each morning using FIFO and record cold-room and display-counter temperature checks twice daily.
• Serve about 120 customers on a Saturday, advising on cuts and cooking times.
• Trained two apprentices in knife handling and cleaning routines.
• Prepared whole lambs and suckling pigs for weddings and family events; the largest order was for a 180-guest wedding.

Counter Assistant | Tržnica Dolac meat hall stall, Zagreb | 2015–2019
• Served customers, weighed and priced orders, and operated the till and cash-up.
• Cleaned and sanitised slicers, mincers and the counter at closing.
• Wrote a closing and cleaning checklist for the stall’s equipment and work areas.

EDUCATION & CERTIFICATES
Vocational certificate: Butcher (3-year programme), Food Trades School Zagreb, 2015
HACCP basic food hygiene certificate, 2021 (renewed 2024)

SKILLS
Carcass breakdown (beef, pork, lamb) · Boning and trimming · Sausage making · Knife sharpening · Mincer and bandsaw operation · FIFO stock rotation · Cold-chain temperature checks · Customer service · Cash handling

LANGUAGES
Croatian (native) · English (good) · German (basic)


COVER LETTER

Dear FreshCart Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Butcher / Meat Counter Assistant position at FreshCart’s Zagreb-Jarun store. I have completed butcher training and bring nine years of experience across a meat counter and a butcher’s shop, combining practical cutting skills with helpful customer service.

In my current role, I break down beef, pork and lamb, bone and portion cuts for the counter, and make fresh sausages to the shop’s recipes. I also rotate stock using FIFO, record temperature checks twice daily and advise customers on suitable cuts and cooking times. On busy Saturdays, I serve about 120 customers. Alongside this, my earlier counter experience included weighing and pricing orders, operating the till, and cleaning and sanitising equipment and work areas.

I hold a basic HACCP food hygiene certificate, renewed in 2024, and take care to maintain accurate checks and hygienic work routines. FreshCart’s emphasis on knowledgeable, honest advice and well-stocked counters fits the way I approach the work: with attention to the product, food safety and each customer’s needs.

I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience could contribute to the Zagreb-Jarun team. Thank you for considering my application.

Kind regards,
Tomislav Mesarić

critique.content_quality_feedback: The actual letter is clear, concise, professional, and well targeted to the Butcher / Meat Counter Assistant role. It presents the strongest relevant evidence: butcher training, nine years of meat-counter and butcher-shop experience, carcass breakdown, sausage making, FIFO rotation, temperature checks, customer advice, till operation, and sanitation. The tone also reflects FreshCart’s emphasis on knowledgeable advice, hygiene, and customer service. However, the document is presented as a full CV followed by a cover letter and begins with the heading “CURRICULUM VITAE,” which is inappropriate for a standalone short letter and creates unnecessary duplication. The letter could also make its practical impact slightly stronger by including one distinctive supported example, such as preparing large wedding orders or handling high-volume Saturday service.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The cover letter uses straightforward headings, standard text, and searchable terms such as “butcher training,” “HACCP,” “FIFO,” “temperature checks,” “fresh sausages,” “customer service,” “till,” and “cleaning and sanitising.” This should support ATS and AI screening for the two must-have requirements. The main parsing and presentation weakness is that the document combines a complete CV with the letter, includes the heading “CURRICULUM VITAE,” and repeats much of the same information. That may confuse document classification and makes the application less aligned with the instruction to submit a short letter. The letter itself has a high probability of passing basic keyword screening, particularly for butcher training and HACCP knowledge, but the combined format moderately reduces professionalism and screening clarity.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: Alignment is strong for the core requirements and most day-to-day duties. The letter demonstrates completed butcher training, more than two years of meat-counter experience, HACCP-related temperature and hygiene checks, cutting and portioning, FIFO stock rotation, customer advice, counter service, cash handling, and equipment cleaning. Its reference to FreshCart’s knowledgeable and honest customer advice is supported by the company information and fits the candidate’s experience advising customers on cuts and cooking times. The candidate’s material shows a gap for the nice-to-have forklift licence: the notes explicitly state that Tomislav has no forklift licence, although he has used a hand pallet jack. The materials also do not show supermarket self-service packaging or tray-sealer/labelling-scale experience; these are role-related differences rather than defects in the letter. The letter appropriately does not claim those skills.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL — In the document before the salutation, remove the entire duplicated CV section, including the “CURRICULUM VITAE” heading, contact block, profile, experience, education, skills, and languages. Retain only the cover-letter section beginning “Dear FreshCart Hiring Team,” so the submitted document is a genuine short letter rather than a combined CV and letter.

MINOR — In the second paragraph of the cover letter, add one distinctive, fully supported result after the sentence about serving 120 customers, for example: “I have also prepared whole lambs and suckling pigs for weddings and family events, including an order of four lambs and two pigs for a 180-guest wedding.” This gives the recruiter memorable evidence of scale and practical responsibility without adding unsupported claims.

MINOR — In the final paragraph, replace “how my experience could contribute to the Zagreb-Jarun team” with a more role-specific phrase such as “how my cutting, counter-service and food-safety experience could contribute to FreshCart’s well-stocked, hygienic meat counter.” This uses the advertisement’s terminology while remaining truthful.
critique.critical_issues: The document is labelled “CURRICULUM VITAE” and contains the complete CV before the cover letter, despite being submitted as a cover letter. This is a document-format and professionalism issue that should be corrected by removing the duplicated CV content and retaining only the short letter. No unsupported skills, tools, qualifications, or experience were detected in the cover-letter text.

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is concise, professional, and well tailored to the Butcher / Meat Counter Assistant role. It presents the strongest relevant evidence: carcass breakdown, boning and portioning, sausage production, FIFO stock rotation, temperature checks, customer advice, high-volume Saturday service, till operation, and hygiene routines. The wedding catering example adds credible scale and impact. The tone also aligns well with FreshCart’s emphasis on knowledgeable advice, hygiene, reliability, and well-stocked counters. The letter is complete and appropriately brief for the employer’s request for a short letter.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter uses clear paragraphs, standard headings are not required for this format, and there are no tables, graphics, columns, or unusual formatting that would interfere with parsing. It includes strong job-relevant terms such as butcher training, beef, pork, lamb, bone, portion, fresh sausages, FIFO, temperature checks, HACCP, customer service, till, cleaning, sanitising, and food safety. ATS and AI screening probability is high because the content is closely aligned with the advertised duties and requirements. A minor improvement would be to use the exact phrase “HACCP knowledge,” since that is the wording in the requirements.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: Alignment is very strong. The document shows completed butcher training and substantially exceeds the minimum two years of meat-counter experience. It demonstrates the core duties of cutting and portioning fresh meat, advising customers on cuts and preparation, rotating stock using FIFO, and recording temperature checks. The candidate’s HACCP certificate and hygiene routines support the food-safety requirement. The letter also reflects FreshCart’s culture through its references to knowledgeable, honest customer advice, product care, hygiene, and customer needs. The candidate does not have the nice-to-have forklift licence, which is a genuine qualification gap rather than a document defect. The candidate’s material also indicates no supermarket experience and no experience with self-service packaging or labelling equipment; these are not stated requirements, but they may be relevant practical differences from the current butcher-shop experience.
critique.improvement_instructions: Minor enhancement: In the third paragraph, change “I hold a basic HACCP food hygiene certificate” to “I hold a basic HACCP food hygiene certificate and have practical HACCP knowledge, including twice-daily temperature and hygiene checks.” This uses the job advertisement’s exact requirement wording while remaining truthful and supported by the candidate’s experience. Keep the existing FIFO, customer-service, and food-safety examples unchanged, as they are already strong evidence for the advertised duties.
critique.critical_issues:
Claims the sources (the candidate's own material; for the employer, the job ad and company research) do not support:
- "maintain accurate checks"

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is concise, professional, and well targeted to the Butcher / Meat Counter Assistant role. It presents relevant qualifications, practical meat-processing experience, customer service, FIFO rotation, HACCP checks, and high-volume Saturday service. The wedding and event preparation example adds credible scale and impact. The closing is appropriate and does not make unsupported claims. One minor opportunity is to name the butcher qualification and school explicitly rather than referring only to “butcher training,” which would make the qualification easier for a recruiter to verify.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter uses several relevant job-description terms, including “butcher training,” “HACCP,” “FIFO,” “temperature checks,” “customer service,” “cuts,” “portion,” “counter,” and “cleaning and sanitising.” Its simple layout and standard paragraphs are parsing-friendly. For stronger ATS and recruiter recognition, the qualification could be written using its exact credential wording: “Vocational certificate: Butcher (3-year programme), Food Trades School Zagreb, 2015.” The document does not contain unusual formatting, tables, graphics, or keyword stuffing. AI screening probability is high because the content is specific, consistent with the candidate information, and supported by concrete quantities and examples.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document strongly demonstrates both must-have requirements: completed butcher training and HACCP knowledge. It also aligns well with the role’s duties by describing cutting, boning, portioning, sausage production, FIFO stock rotation, temperature checks, customer advice, counter service, and equipment sanitation. The customer-focused language fits FreshCart’s emphasis on knowledgeable, honest advice and helpful service. Minor enhancement: In the third paragraph, change “I hold a basic HACCP food hygiene certificate, renewed in 2024” to “I hold a basic HACCP food hygiene certificate issued in 2021 and renewed in 2024.” This preserves the truthful level of the certificate while presenting the credential more precisely.
